messages:
Alex V.: heads up — after last night's firmware batch some eu-west1 racks are showing IPMI connection queueing and a handful of nodes toggled secure boot on during the update. noticing ~10% of GPU nodes come up as 'inaccessible' during provisioning :grimace:
Priya K.: ugh. which batch? rack ids? any pattern (hw sku, fw rev)?
Alex V.: rollout id fw-roll-2026-03-17, racks: rw-eu-03/04/07. fw revs bumped from 2.1.9 -> 2.2.0. pattern: BMCs with older IPMI stacks (ipmi v2 fallback) hitting connection limit when we run concurrent oob tasks
Jamal: on it. grabbing BMC logs now. if IPMI sessions queue up, the autoscaler gets blocked waiting for node readiness which then spikes pending pods and duplicate scale attempts. cost will climb if we keep autoscaler thrashing.
Alex V.: exact. noticed burst of provisioning retries in the console and a couple of reclaim cycles. we should pause remaining eu-west batches until we confirm a fix.
eng-oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0317-02 — "IPMI session queueing + secure boot drift in eu-west1". Severity: P2. Pager notified: @eng-oncall.
Priya K.: suggested immediate mitigation: 1) pause fw rollout 2) apply temporary IPMI session-rate limit on the orchestration side 3) if nodes show secure boot enabled unexpectedly, mask them from autoscaler pool and boot to maintenance.
Emilia: how do we mask quickly? can we tag nodes?
Jamal: yes — tag with label `oob:maintenance` and the autoscaler exclude rule will skip. I'll run a quick script to label the current set:```
# label affected nodes
kubectl get nodes -l zone=eu-west1 -o name | grep rw-eu | xargs -I{} kubectl label {} oob=maintenance --overwrite
```
Carlos: thanks. once labeled we should also throttle concurrent IPMI connections from the orchestrator. short-term throttle: reduce concurrency from 40 -> 8 for eu-west pools.
Alex V.: agreed. Jamal, can you share the exact ipmitool command you use to probe BMC sessions? want to audit open sessions across racks.
Jamal: use `ipmitool -I lanplus -H $BMC -U admin -P **** sol info` to check active sessions; and `ipmitool -I lanplus -H $BMC -U admin -P **** mc info` for firmware info. also watching `/var/log/bmc.log` for `session_alloc` errors.
Priya K.: if secure boot flipped during the update we need to check the BIOS payload; maybe the update toggled the UEFI variable. can we compare NVRAM vars across before/after snapshots?
Alex V.: yes — we have nvram snapshots for those racks from pre-rollout. Jamal please run nvram diff and upload to the incident.
Jamal: will do. running diffs now. also queued an OOB BMC restart for two most noisy nodes, doing one-at-a-time per runbook: `runbook: oob/bmc-restart-v2`
Emilia: any user-facing impact? are customer jobs failing?
Alex V.: small surface area so far — some teams saw job startup delays. no data plane failures. but if autoscaler keeps retrying we hit cost windows. notified support to hold on escalations.
Carlos: long-term: we should add pre-flight checks to the firmware pipeline that verify IPMI session behaviour and secure-boot NV state on a canary host before mass rollout. also add a rollback job that ensures NV match.
Priya K.: +1. for now: pausing remaining eu-west fw jobs (Alex), reducing orchestrator IPMI concurrency (Carlos), labeling affected nodes (Jamal), upload nvram diffs and BMC logs to INC ticket (Jamal). anyone want to pick up postmortem?
Emilia: I can own the postmortem and runbook updates.
Alex V.: thanks. I'll post a short summary to #incidents once we have the nvram diffs and the results of the one-at-a-time restarts. :thumbsup:
